Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 536 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2018) 
 
 
Introduction 
Wildlife Management Unit 536 is an area of boreal forest located in NW Alberta. WMU 536 holds resident 
populations of moose, bison, caribou and limited numbers of white-tailed deer. The WMU is very important for 
Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal hunting interests. 
 
Survey Method 
Alberta Environment and Parks conducted an aerial ungulate survey in February 2018 to provide an updated 
estimate on ungulate populations within the WMU. The survey was conducted using Distance Sampling 
methodology utilizing two Bell 206 Jet Rangers from February 12 -15th. Transects were flown at an altitude of 300 
feet at a speed of 60-80 knots. 
 
Results 
Survey crews flew 198 transects for a total of 1,909 kilometers and 39.4 flight hours. While on transect the crews 
observed 168 moose (79 cows, 48 calves, 36 bulls and 1 unclassified). The population estimate and density 
information is found in (Table 1). The Bull:Cow:Calf ratio was calculated to be 51:100:61

Discussion 
The moose population in WMU 536 appear to be stable compared to previous surveys, and the population 
estimate is close to the 2017 preseason population estimate. The bull: cow ratio shows continued bull availability 
and is consistent with other survey results for the WMU. Moose calf recruitment is greater than expected (61 
calves: 100 cows) for a northern boreal WMU, indicating good productivity in the population and potential for 
growth if overwinter calf survival is high.
